subject.title: feat(skills): declarative cron-trigger metadata in SKILL.md frontmatter

question: Should OpenClaw allow SKILL.md metadata to declare autonomous scheduled or event-triggered execution, and if so what permission, provenance, approval, and revocation contract must gate it?
rationale: This would create a public skill metadata contract that can cause future agent runs, so automation cannot safely choose the product and security boundary from source shape alone.

options.title: Define Permissioned Trigger Contract
options.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers specify a guarded SKILL.md trigger contract covering trusted sources, operator approval, scheduler registration, event names, last-triggered state, and revocation.

options.title: Route To Explicit Cron/Plugin APIs
options.body: Reject SKILL.md-owned autonomous triggers and require skills or plugins to document explicit operator-created cron jobs or maintainer-approved plugin hooks instead.

options.title: Metadata-Only First
options.body: Allow a non-executing documentation field such as trigger_description for audits while deferring automatic cron/event registration to a later security review.

recommendation.title: Define Permissioned Trigger Contract
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers specify a guarded SKILL.md trigger contract covering trusted sources, operator approval, scheduler registration, event names, last-triggered state, and revocation.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice spans skill metadata, cron automation, ClawHub/plugin boundaries, and security defaults, and steipete is the strongest current-history routing signal for those areas.
